JACK RATHBONE, who has performed with credit in our teams in the past, retired at the three-quarter distance, but he is determined that next year he will get right there—and in good time, too!
Charlie Speechley was also speedy, but not quite fast enough to catch Veteran Jack Rathbone, who made good use of his five minutes allowance to finish second.

Composed of men who have many years of walking in front of them (with the possible exception of Jack Rathbone), they gained valuable experience, and showed that in our reserve ranks we have some who will shortly be qualifying for first team places.
Three members of this team were destined to be in the winning team the following year; and Jack Rathbone was in our winning "Senior" team later in the season.

Memories of Brighton Walks with Tommy Green, Fred Rickards and Fred Bentley to the fore, followed by many other stalwarts; of National 20-Miles Championships with George Cooper, Bob McMullen (Senior), Stanley Manning. Jack Rathbone. Joe King, Jack Bidgood and others, striving their utmost.

Jack Rathbone, one of our long-distance walking stalwarts of some dozen or so years ago, sends greetings to his old friends and invites any of them to call on him for a cup of tea and a yarn if they are down Herne Bay way, where he now has a place of his own.
